column3: “He is highly exalted” renders an emphatic doubled verb, “being exalted he is exalted”; “hurled” renders “thrown.”
“song” renders a word that can also mean “might”; “praise” renders “glorify (adorn).”
NASB uses the present “overthrow … send … consumes” where the Hebrew has past and narrative forms; “burning anger” renders “anger (burning).”
“My desire shall be gratified against them” renders “my soul shall be full of them,” and “destroy” renders “dispossess.”
Close to the Hebrew; “He is highly exalted” renders the doubled verb as in verse 1.
“for them” and “tested them” render the singular “for it” and “tested it” (the people).
“give earnest heed” renders an emphatic doubled verb, “listening you will listen”; “your healer” renders “who heals you.”
